crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Finding acquisition targets is the front end of private equity and deal sourcing, where a firm turns an investment thesis into a list of companies worth contacting. It covers market mapping, sector screens, ownership research, growth signals, and fit with fund strategy. Public filings, such as the 393 merger and acquisition filings tracked on this site, are one input among many. The work is not just search, it is continuous pipeline building and prioritization.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on a mix of commercial databases, company registries, news and filing feeds, CRM systems, and internal data warehouses. Teams often combine structured fields, such as revenue, headcount, and ownership, with unstructured text from websites, press releases, and interviews. Search and matching tools help deduplicate records and link entities across sources. Cloud storage and APIs let analysts refresh screens and share lists across deal teams.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: A typical process starts with a thesis that defines sector, size, geography, and value creation angle. Analysts then build a long list from databases, filings, trade press, conferences, and referrals, and score each target on strategic fit, financial profile, and likelihood of a transaction. Machine learning can rank and cluster companies, flag similar businesses, and monitor triggers such as leadership changes, funding rounds, or facility expansions. Human review remains central because relationship history, reputation, and owner intent are hard to model. The output is a prioritized pipeline that feeds outreach and preliminary diligence.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Data used in sourcing is expected to come from lawful sources with clear rights for commercial use. Personal data, confidential board materials, and material non public information require controls, and teams often keep audit trails of what was collected, when, and from where. Bias in screening can narrow the pipeline or expose the firm to reputational harm, so diverse sourcing and documented criteria matter. Litigation and regulatory exposure can also surface during screening, and this site tracks 149 active AI lawsuits and 222 compliance and regulation pages as reference points. The governance goal is repeatable, defensible sourcing that respects contracts, privacy, and market conduct rules.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Sourcing is moving toward continuous monitoring rather than periodic list building. AI agents and large language models are being tested to read filings, summarize calls, and draft outreach, while graph analytics map ownership and supply chain links. More integration between deal databases, CRM, and portfolio monitoring is likely, with alerts when a target shows a relevant change. The limiting factors will be data rights, model reliability, and the judgment needed to interpret owner motivations. The field will likely keep the human relationship at the center even as the search becomes faster and more automated.
